title: Validation & integrity: output validators, fixtures, CI
description:
The repo lints the prompt *templates* (the "recipe") but never the generated pass *outputs* (the "dish"). `tools/lint_pass_templates.py` has a full fixture suite over the seven prompt templates, yet there is zero validation on the output side — even though the project names `downstream-analysis-passes` and `downstream-extraction-tools` as audiences and says the structured schema exists "to make path-bearing fields routable by later tools." The LLM-authored YAML appendix (indentation-sensitive, enum-bearing, hand-emitted) is precisely the fragile artifact that breaks consumers silently.

This epic lands seven validation/integrity interventions that close that asymmetry: a stable output-extraction marker, a new output validator, golden+bad output fixtures and a harness, a meta-lint guaranteeing per-field fixture coverage, two new template-linter checks (frontmatter consistency, no-future-pass anticipation), and a CI workflow that makes all of it unconditional on every push/PR. Nothing here reaches analytical quality — every check is a structural property of template or output text, the same remit the existing linter already lives within.
design:
Branch `validation-integrity` off `main`; squash-merge at end. One commit per deliverable (or cohesive sub-step) for bisect resolution, ordered bisect bottom-up so a green build certifies the whole stack:
1. Output extraction marker: schema doc + seven template skeletons + version bumps (#4).
2. Template-linter extensions: frontmatter consistency (#5) + no-future-pass rule (#1) + their template fixtures.
3. Output validator `tools/lint_pass_outputs.py` (#2) — the import shim lands inline here, not as a separate commit.
4. Output fixtures + output fixture harness (#3).
5. Meta-lint coverage test (#6).
6. CI workflow (#7).

Ordering rationale: #4 lands before #2 so the validator can key off the marker rather than the weaker `pass_output:`-first-key heuristic; #2 before #3 because fixtures are test data *for* the validator; #6 after #3 because the meta-lint asserts coverage *of* those fixtures; #7 last because it runs everything.
acceptance_criteria:
- All seven child deliverables are landed and merged.
- CI is green: every linter exits 0 on the real templates and good fixtures, exits non-zero on every bad fixture, and the meta-lint reports full field coverage.
- The existing `tools/lint_pass_templates.py` remains byte-for-byte unchanged except for the two newly appended checks (frontmatter consistency, no-future-pass) — Decision A keeps the output validator from editing it.
- Deliberately NOT added (do not "helpfully" introduce): formal JSON Schema, worked-example gallery, output provenance / `template_version` / `passes.json`.

title: Add stable output extraction marker
description: Downstream tools need to locate the `pass_output` YAML block in a completed analysis unambiguously. Today the only contract is implicit: "the first ```yaml fence whose first key is `pass_output:`" — the heuristic baked into `pass_output_block` in `tools/lint_pass_templates.py`. That is fragile and ambiguous if an output ever carries two `pass_output` blocks. A stable, machine-greppable marker makes extraction robust for any consumer.
design:
Decision B — a single one-line HTML-comment sentinel `<!-- repo-review:pass_output -->` on the line immediately above the fenced `pass_output` block, carried in each template's appendix skeleton so every emitted output inherits it. HTML comments survive Markdown rendering, are trivial to regex, and add exactly one line per template. Opening sentinel only — no closing sentinel (the fence already closes unambiguously).

Steps:
- Document the convention in `STRUCTURED_OUTPUT_SCHEMA.md`: a new short (~8-line) section after the intro stating the sentinel string, that it immediately precedes the `pass_output` fence, and that consumers should prefer it and fall back to the `pass_output:`-key heuristic for older markerless outputs.
- Add the sentinel line above the `pass_output` fence in all seven template appendix skeletons: `01-first-read.md`, `02-discounted-artifact.md`, `02.5-synthesis.md`, `03-trace.md`, `04-twin.md`, `05-lift.md`, `06-delta-review.md`.
- Do NOT add marker-aware extraction to `lint_pass_templates.py` (Decision A keeps it byte-for-byte unchanged). The marker-aware locator lives only in the new output validator (sibling deliverable). The template linter's existing heuristic still finds the fence whether or not the sentinel is present, so older markerless fixtures keep validating.
- Version-bump the seven edited templates' frontmatter `version:` per project convention: `06-delta-review.md` 2→3; the other six 5→6. One atomic commit for the bumps.
acceptance_criteria:
- `STRUCTURED_OUTPUT_SCHEMA.md` documents the sentinel `<!-- repo-review:pass_output -->`, its placement (immediately above the `pass_output` fence), and the prefer-marker / fall-back-to-heuristic consumer guidance.
- All seven templates carry the sentinel line immediately above their `pass_output` fence.
- All seven edited templates have bumped `version:` (`06-delta-review.md`→3, the other six→6).
- `tools/lint_pass_templates.py` is unchanged; `python3 tools/lint_pass_templates.py` and `python3 tests/run_pass_template_lint_tests.py` still exit 0.

title: Add frontmatter consistency lint
description: Template frontmatter can drift out of internal consistency in ways nothing currently catches: a `pass_id` that disagrees with its filename, a prerequisite naming a non-existent pass, or a non-integer `version`. `tools/lint_pass_templates.py` has `has_frontmatter` but does not parse frontmatter fields, so these errors ship silently.
design:
Three new checks appended to `tools/lint_pass_templates.py`, run over the seven templates and wired into `validate_path` alongside the existing checks. Stdlib only; emit failures in the existing `<file>:<line>: <detail>` format.

1. **`pass_id` ↔ filename.** Strip the numeric sequence prefix (`NN-` or `NN.N-`) and the `.md` suffix from the basename; the remainder must equal `pass_id`. Grounded: `01-first-read.md`→`first-read`, `02.5-synthesis.md`→`synthesis`, `06-delta-review.md`→`delta-review`. All seven currently satisfy this.
2. **Prerequisites resolve.** Every entry in `prerequisites` *and* `recommended_prerequisites` must be a known `pass_id` from the canonical set `{first-read, discounted-artifact, synthesis, trace, twin, lift, delta-review}`.
3. **`version` is an int.** The frontmatter `version:` value must parse as a base-10 integer.

Implementation: add a small stdlib frontmatter scanner that returns the lines between the first two `---` markers, plus helpers to read a scalar (`version`, `pass_id`) and a simple indentation-based block-list (`prerequisites`, `recommended_prerequisites`).

Fixtures (register expect-fail in `tests/run_pass_template_lint_tests.py`'s `CASES`): `bad-frontmatter-passid-filename-mismatch.md`, `bad-frontmatter-unknown-prerequisite.md`, `bad-frontmatter-version-not-int.md`.
acceptance_criteria:
- `tools/lint_pass_templates.py` enforces the three checks and emits `<file>:<line>: <detail>` failures.
- All seven real templates still pass.
- The three new bad fixtures exist under `tests/fixtures/pass-template-lint/` and are registered expect-fail in `CASES`; each causes a non-zero exit.
- `python3 tests/run_pass_template_lint_tests.py` exits 0 (every case meets expectation).
notes: CLOSED. Added frontmatter_block/scalar/list helpers + frontmatter_failures to lint_pass_templates.py; three checks (pass_id<->filename gated on NN- prefix, prerequisites resolve, version int) wired into validate_path. 3 expect-fail fixtures isolate each check; real templates + full harness exit 0. Commit eb1bf34.

title: Add no-future-pass anticipation lint
description: The methodology's single load-bearing taste rule is "no pass anticipates a later pass." Every base-sequence pass states it in prose but nothing enforces it. This is not hypothetical: synthesis prose naming Trace/Twin/Lift was found and hand-fixed in past work. A mechanical guard catches forward references at author time. This is the highest-confidence item in the set.
design:
A new check in `tools/lint_pass_templates.py`: a base-sequence template must not name, in its **prose**, any pass that comes later in the series. Stdlib only; emit `<file>:<line>: names later pass '<Display Name>'`, exit 1 on any hit.

Canonical series order (NOT the prerequisite DAG): `0 first-read  1 discounted-artifact  2 synthesis  3 trace  4 twin  5 lift`. `06-delta-review` is exempt (out-of-band; references nothing forward). For the template at index *i*, the forbidden set is every pass at index > *i*.

What counts as "naming" a later pass (match against prose only), two token classes:
- **Proper-noun display names**, case-sensitive, whole-word: `The Trace`/`Trace`, `The Twin`/`Twin`, `The Lift`/`Lift`, `The Synthesis`/`Synthesis`, `The Discounted Artifact`/`Discounted Artifact`, `The First Read`/`First Read`.
- **`pass_id` tokens** in reference position: matched inside backticks, or as a bare hyphenated id (`discounted-artifact`, `first-read`, `delta-review`). For the single-word ids (`trace`, `twin`, `lift`, `synthesis`) match the backticked form ONLY, never the bare lowercase word — the explicit guard against false positives on the verbs "trace"/"lift"/"twin".

Critical exclusions (or the rule fires on legitimate text):
- Skip the frontmatter block.
- Skip ALL fenced ``` blocks. Load-bearing: the shared `coverage_closure` skeleton's `chosen_from_pass` enum legitimately lists later passes (e.g. `03-trace`'s appendix enum lists `twin`) because the skeleton is shared across trace/twin/lift. Scanning fenced blocks would guarantee a false positive on every trace/twin/lift template.

Pre-flight (MANDATORY, do this first): run the rule against the seven real templates before writing fixtures. Post-cleanup they are expected to pass. If any real template trips it, that is either (a) a genuine forward reference to fix in prose — a real finding, surface it, do not silently exempt — or (b) a construct needing a documented exclusion. Resolve before shipping the rule green.

Fixtures (register in `CASES`): `good-synthesis-no-forward-ref.md` (clean) and `bad-synthesis-names-trace.md` (prose says e.g. "what Trace should test").
acceptance_criteria:
- `tools/lint_pass_templates.py` implements the rule with the two token classes and both exclusions (frontmatter + all fenced blocks), emitting `<file>:<line>: names later pass '<Display Name>'`.
- The rule passes against all seven real templates (pre-flight done; any real forward-reference surfaced and resolved in prose, not silently exempted).
- `good-synthesis-no-forward-ref.md` and `bad-synthesis-names-trace.md` exist and are registered in `CASES` (good expect-pass, bad expect-fail); the harness exits 0.
- No false positive on the verbs trace/lift/twin or on the shared `coverage_closure` enum inside fenced blocks.
notes: CLOSED. forward_reference_failures + prose_lines added to lint_pass_templates.py. Pre-flight against 7 real templates: CLEAN (0 hits, no false positives on verbs/enum). Positive control confirms it catches display names + backticked ids while ignoring bare verbs. good-synthesis-no-forward-ref (pass) + bad-synthesis-names-trace (fail) in CASES. Harness exit 0. Commit 43b7e11.

title: Add output validator lint_pass_outputs.py
description: There is no validation of a completed analysis's filled-in `pass_output` block — only the template skeletons are linted. The LLM-emitted YAML appendix carries real values (enums, paths, nested blocks) that can be malformed in ways that silently break downstream consumers. This validator is the core deliverable; everything else orbits it. The template linter checks *field presence* in a skeleton of `<placeholder>` values; this validator checks **real values**: required fields present AND enum membership AND type/shape correctness. Same parser, stronger assertions.
design:
New `tools/lint_pass_outputs.py`, a sibling to the template linter. Stdlib only. CLI: `python3 tools/lint_pass_outputs.py <file>...`, same exit semantics and `<file>:<line>: <detail>` output format as the template linter. Top-of-file docstring states it validates *generated outputs* (mirror of the template linter's "validates templates, not outputs").

Import shim (Decision A — part of THIS deliverable, not a separate step). Reuse the template linter's parsing primitives via a two-line path shim at the top of the new file; the template linter stays byte-for-byte unchanged:

    import sys
    from pathlib import Path
    sys.path.insert(0, str(Path(__file__).resolve().parent))
    import lint_pass_templates as tmpl

Reused primitives: `yaml_fenced_blocks`, `pass_output_block`, `value_for_key`, `fields_under`, `block_has_fields`, `indent_of`, `source_notes_lines`, `path_field_failures`; constants `SOURCE_FIELDS`, `PATH_KEYS`, `SMALLEST_OPEN_FIELDS`, `COVERAGE_CLOSURE_FIELDS`, `PATH_RE`.

Checks:
1. **Locate** the `pass_output` block: an own `locate_pass_output` that scans for the `<!-- repo-review:pass_output -->` sentinel first, then falls back to the imported `pass_output_block` heuristic (older markerless outputs).
2. **`pass_id`** present and in the canonical set; dispatch the rest by it.
3. **Required fields per `pass_id`** — a `REQUIRED` map covering the SHARED SUBSTRATE ONLY (Decision C), reusing `SOURCE_FIELDS`, `SMALLEST_OPEN_FIELDS`, `COVERAGE_CLOSURE_FIELDS`, plus one new constant the template linter lacks: `CONFIDENCE_FIELDS = (overall, blind_spots, smallest_open)` (the template linter models only `smallest_open` inside `confidence`, not the full block). Pass-class sets: `SINGLE_REPO_PASSES`, `SMALLEST_OPEN_PASSES`, `COVERAGE_CLOSURE_PASSES`, and twin/delta-review's dual source-state blocks. description: The output validator needs test data and a harness proving good-passes / bad-fails, paralleling the existing ~19-fixture template suite. title: Add CI workflow running all checks
description: Today the linters and harnesses exist but fire only when a human remembers to run them. CI makes all of it unconditional — every check runs on every push and pull request, so structural drift in templates or outputs fails the build automatically. This lands last so a green build certifies the whole stack.
design:
New `.github/workflows/ci.yml` (the `.github/workflows/` directory does not exist yet — create it). ~25 lines, stdlib only; no dependencies beyond `python3`.

    name: ci
    on: [push, pull_request]
    jobs:
      lint:
        runs-on: ubuntu-latest
        steps:
          - uses: actions/checkout@v4
          - uses: actions/setup-python@v5
            with: { python-version: '3.x' }
          - run: python3 tools/lint_pass_templates.py
          - run: python3 tests/run_pass_template_lint_tests.py
          - run: python3 tools/lint_pass_outputs.py tests/fixtures/pass-output-lint/good-*.md
          - run: python3 tests/run_pass_output_lint_tests.py
          - run: python3 tests/run_fixture_coverage_meta_test.py

Any non-zero exit fails the build. The bare `lint_pass_outputs.py good-*.md` step is a fast canary that the golden fixtures validate clean, independent of the harness; the harness steps prove good-passes/bad-fails; the meta step proves coverage completeness. The repo is public, so Actions minutes are free; `setup-python` is convenience (the job would also work on the runner's system Python).
acceptance_criteria:
- `.github/workflows/ci.yml` exists, triggers on `[push, pull_request]`, and runs all five check steps in order.
- A non-zero exit from any step fails the build.
- Lands last, after the other six deliverables, so a green build certifies the whole stack.

title: Output provenance + human pass-map
description:
This delivers the deferred Top-5 idea #5 (output provenance + a machine-readable pass manifest) — but in the project's **human-facing idiom**, not as JSON. Two gaps motivate it. (1) **Outputs carry no provenance:** a completed `pass_output` appendix records the pass's identity, timestamp, and source-state provenance, but **not** which template version produced it; after the recent schema churn (base templates now at `version: 6`, delta-review at `3`) a consumer cannot tell a pre-churn output from a post-churn one. (2) **The series' shape lives in seven frontmatters:** learning the DAG (who depends on whom, which passes stop early, what each catches, current versions) means grepping all seven.

The governing principle for the reframing: **the agentic face must speak the human face's idiom — prose, Markdown, or YAML. JSON is the boundary.** So provenance becomes one field in the existing YAML appendix, and the manifest becomes a readable `PASSES.md` (table + DAG) that is a drift-checked *view* of the frontmatters rather than a generated `passes.json`. This also folds in the undone "pass-map diagram" idea.
design:
**Workflow (per the V&I handoff correction): solo, directly on `main`, ONE commit for the whole cycle, then push. No feature branch.** (The prior V&I cycle was mistakenly started on a branch and collapsed back to one `main` commit; do not repeat that. `git bisect` localizing a regression to "the whole cycle" is the accepted trade.)

Internal build order within the single commit, bisect-bottom-up so each step rests on the last:
1. `template_version` in the seven appendix skeletons + schema-doc section + version bumps (d1).
2. Template-linter drift guard appendix==frontmatter + its template fixtures (d2).
3. Output validator required+int check + output fixtures + meta-lint update (d3).
4. `PASSES.md` authored to match current frontmatters (d4).
5. `tools/lint_pass_map.py` drift guard (d5).
6. Pass-map fixtures + harness (d6).
7. CI lines + README pointer (d7), last, so a green build certifies the whole stack.

Half A = d1–d3 (provenance), the load-bearing/timely half. Half B = d4–d6 (pass-map). d7 is the glue.

title: Add template_version provenance field to appendix skeletons

title: Require template_version in output validator and meta-lint
description: The output validator (`tools/lint_pass_outputs.py`) does not yet require `template_version`, so a completed output could omit the new provenance field and still validate. It should enforce presence and integer type. Separately, the per-field coverage meta-lint covers only block sub-fields: `pass_id` (a required *top-level* field) already sits outside it, and `template_version` would be a second uncovered top-level field — making "one bad fixture per required field" incoherent unless both are pulled into one model.

Three coherent sub-parts.

(a) **Validator.** In `tools/lint_pass_outputs.py` add `template_version` to the required top-level `pass_output` fields; check it is present and parses as a base-10 int; emit the standard `<file>:<line>:` failure. (b) **Output fixtures** under `tests/fixtures/pass-output-lint/`: `bad-output-missing-template-version.md`, `bad-output-template-version-not-int.md`, and `bad-output-missing-pass-id.md` (the latter closing the latent top-level-field gap). The validator must emit a specific "missing `pass_id`" failure *before* attempting `pass_id` dispatch, so `bad-output-missing-pass-id.md` fails for its named reason. title: Author PASSES.md human pass-map
description: The series' shape — who depends on whom, which passes stop early, what each catches, current versions — is scattered across seven frontmatters; there is an informal README table but nothing keeps it honest. A single readable `PASSES.md` gives humans a map and agents an index: the human-faced replacement for the rejected `passes.json`, folding in the undone pass-map-diagram idea. The frontmatters remain the single source of truth; `PASSES.md` is a drift-checked view (guarded by d5).
design:
New file `PASSES.md` at repo root, two Markdown parts.

1. **A table**, one row per pass, columns: `pass_id | name | version | prerequisites | recommended | output_kind | terminates_early_when | catches`. The first seven columns are machine-derivable from frontmatter and are what the d5 lint guards; `catches` is human prose (one line, seeded from the README's existing table) and is NOT guarded.
2. **A Mermaid `graph LR` DAG** of the prerequisite graph (hard `prerequisites` as solid edges, `recommended_prerequisites` as dashed). Illustrative and NOT separately drift-guarded — the table is the authoritative guarded surface.

**Table serialization contract (normative — author and linter both obey it):**
- Empty list cell (`prerequisites: []` or no `recommended_prerequisites`) renders as a single em dash `—`; the linter treats `—`/blank as the empty list.
- Non-empty list cell renders as items joined by **comma + single space**, in **frontmatter order**.
- List comparison is **order-insensitive**: split the cell on commas, trim each token, drop a lone `—`, compare as token **sets**.
- Scalar cells (`version`, `output_kind`, `terminates_early_when`, `name`) compared as exact strings after trimming.
- The linter trims outer whitespace on every cell and ignores the header and `---|---` separator rows; pipe-splitting handles leading/trailing `|`.

Initial content grounded in current frontmatter (post-d1 versions): `first-read` v7 (prereqs —, rec —, never); `discounted-artifact` v7 (first-read; —; never); `synthesis` v7 (first-read, discounted-artifact; —; never); `trace` v7 (first-read, discounted-artifact; —; repo-has-no-load-bearing-obligation); `twin` v7 (first-read, discounted-artifact, trace; —; never); `lift` v7 (first-read, discounted-artifact, trace; twin; repo-yields-no-extractables); `delta-review` v4 (first-read; discounted-artifact, synthesis, trace, twin, lift; never).

- `PASSES.md` exists at repo root with the eight-column table covering all seven passes and a Mermaid prerequisite DAG.
- Every machine-derivable cell matches current frontmatter per the serialization contract (empty→`—`, non-empty→comma+space frontmatter-order).
- The table obeys the normative serialization contract exactly (so the d5 lint can parse it).
- No canonical prompt prose changed. (The README pointer is handled by d7.)

title: Add tools/lint_pass_map.py drift guard
description: `PASSES.md` is hand-authored and will drift from the frontmatters over time (a version bump, a new prerequisite). A lint must guarantee the map stays in sync with the single source of truth — the seven template frontmatters.
design:
New `tools/lint_pass_map.py`, stdlib-only line scanner.

**CLI:** `python3 tools/lint_pass_map.py [pass_map_path]` — the pass-map path is **positional and optional**, default `<repo-root>/PASSES.md`. The seven real template frontmatters are **always** read from repo root (resolved as `Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent`), independent of `pass_map_path`. This split — table from the argument, frontmatters always from the real templates — is what lets a bad fixture supply only a divergent table.

Reuse `lint_pass_templates.py`'s frontmatter parser via the **same two-line `sys.path` import shim** that `lint_pass_outputs.py` uses (`import lint_pass_templates as tmpl`); do NOT extract a shared module (keeps the fixture-trusted template linter byte-for-byte unchanged). Parse the `PASSES.md` table with a small pipe-row scanner (split on `|`, strip, skip header/separator rows), honoring the d4 serialization contract.

**Checks:**
1. Every canonical `pass_id` appears in the table exactly once; no unknown `pass_id`. (Messages must contain the literal tokens `missing` / `unknown` so a harness can key on them.)
2. For each pass, the table's `version`, `prerequisites`, `recommended`, `output_kind`, `terminates_early_when`, and `name` match frontmatter (list columns order-insensitive by token set).

Emit `PASSES.md: <pass_id>: <column> says X, frontmatter says Y` on drift — the `<column>` token is the substring a harness asserts on. Exit non-zero on any mismatch.
acceptance_criteria:
- `tools/lint_pass_map.py` exists; `python3 tools/lint_pass_map.py` (no argument) exits 0 against the real `PASSES.md` and frontmatters.
- It reads frontmatters from repo root regardless of the pass-map path argument.
- Drift in any guarded column (`version`/`prerequisites`/`recommended`/`output_kind`/`terminates_early_when`/`name`) produces a `<pass_id>: <column> says X, frontmatter says Y` failure and non-zero exit; missing/unknown-pass messages contain the literal `missing`/`unknown` tokens.
- Reuses the template linter's parser via the import shim; `lint_pass_templates.py` unchanged; stdlib only.
close_reason: Added tools/lint_pass_map.py: stdlib pipe-table scanner that drift-checks PASSES.md against the seven template frontmatters. CLI takes an optional positional pass_map_path (default <repo-root>/PASSES.md); frontmatters are ALWAYS read from repo root via REPO_ROOT, independent of the arg. Reuses lint_pass_templates parser through the same two-line sys.path import shim as lint_pass_outputs.py (no shared module extracted; template linter untouched by this file). Check 1: each canonical pass exactly once + no unknown (messages carry literal 'missing'/'unknown'). Check 2: version/name/output_kind/terminates_early_when (scalar exact) and prerequisites/recommended (order-insensitive token set) match frontmatter, emitting '<pass_id>: <column> says X, frontmatter says Y'. No-arg run exits 0 against real PASSES.md; all four drift modes verified. Lands in the single op-pm cycle commit.

title: Add pass-map fixtures and harness
description: The pass-map lint needs negative test data and a harness proving each guarded check actually fires — at the per-check specificity the repo's other negative suites have, not merely a non-zero exit (which could pass for the wrong reason and stop proving its named guard).
design:
New directory `tests/fixtures/pass-map-lint/`, each file containing ONLY a Markdown table (the lint parses nothing else). Each bad fixture diverges in one named column, with the substring it must provoke:
- `bad-pass-map-stale-version.md` — a version cell disagreeing with frontmatter → asserts `version`.
- `bad-pass-map-missing-pass.md` — a `pass_id` absent from the table → asserts `missing`.
- `bad-pass-map-unknown-pass.md` — a row for a non-existent pass → asserts `unknown`.
- `bad-pass-map-wrong-prerequisite.md` — a prerequisites cell drifting from frontmatter → asserts `prerequisites`.

There is **no `good-pass-map.md` copy** — the positive case is the real `PASSES.md` run with the default path argument (as the no-future-pass rule uses the seven real templates as its implicit good case).

New harness `tests/run_pass_map_lint_tests.py`, a near-clone of the output-lint harness: a `CASES` list of `(path, should_pass, expect_substring)`; run `lint_pass_map.py` as a subprocess per case; assert the exit code AND, for bad cases, that captured output contains `expect_substring`. One **good** case invokes the lint with **no path argument** (real `PASSES.md`, expect exit 0, no substring); the four **bad** cases pass a fixture path plus their column substring.

Rationale: substring assertion keeps each fixture *proving its own guard* (if the linter ever stopped validating `prerequisites`, `bad-pass-map-wrong-prerequisite.md` would stop emitting the `prerequisites` substring and the test would go red) while staying churn-free (a future version bump adds drift messages but never removes a fixture's target substring).
acceptance_criteria:
- `tests/fixtures/pass-map-lint/` contains the four table-only bad fixtures.
- `tests/run_pass_map_lint_tests.py` registers one good case (no-arg, expect pass, no substring) and the four bad cases (fixture path + column substring), asserting both exit code and substring.
- `python3 tests/run_pass_map_lint_tests.py` exits 0; each bad fixture fails for its named reason (its target substring is present in the output).

Added tests/run_pass_map_lint_tests.py: near-clone of the output-lint harness with (path, should_pass, expect_substring) CASES — one good no-arg case (real PASSES.md, exit 0, no substring) + four bad cases asserting BOTH non-zero exit AND the column substring, so each fixture proves its own guard. No good-pass-map copy (real PASSES.md is the positive case). Harness exits 0; each bad fixture fails for its named reason. Lands in the single op-pm cycle commit.

title: Rebuild rr-run in Go with config files, batches, and saved sessions
description:
rr-run (tools/rr-run/rr-run.sh, a 106-line Bash script) runs the six repo-review passes (01, 02, 02.5, 03, 04, 05) against one repository through one Claude agent pane controlled by the Gashki CLI. Three needs are unmet.

1. Fragile implementation. Agent arguments are built by concatenating JSON strings. File and linter arguments rely on shell word splitting. sed replacement characters can corrupt a rendered path. The Gashki event-log path comes from an environment variable. The result of the approval-change wait is never checked.
2. No systematic configuration. Four environment variables (RR_MODEL, RR_WAIT, RR_PROMPTS, GASHKI) are the only settings. There is no config file, no record of where a value came from, and no saved record of what a run used.
3. No batches and no way to resume the conversation. One run handles one repository. The Claude session ID is not saved anywhere: Gashki's hook mapper discards the vendor session_id, and Gashki spawn/observe data identify a pane, not a Claude session. A human cannot reopen the review session later to discuss the results with the agent.

This epic converts rr-run to Go (same six-pass review process and prompts), adds layered TOML configuration, adds sequential multi-repository batches, and saves Claude session references so the original review session can be reopened later. It ships in three phases. A phase is a completion checkpoint, not a separate planning cycle, live agent run, publication or release. The phases can be built in one development round, but each phase must pass its checks before dependent work starts.
design:
Phases: (1) convert the current runner with explicit corrections and a persistent run record; (2) replace env settings with layered TOML config and saved config records; (3) add batches, unique per-run artifacts, and saved/reopenable sessions.

Implementation is a separate Go module under tools/rr-run/ (Go 1.26.1 or a later compatible patch, matching the Gashki module's language baseline). Layout:

- go.mod, go.sum
- cmd/rr-run/main.go
- internal/cli: parse declared commands, render human or JSON output
- internal/config: typed settings, file validation, source tracking
- internal/gashki: run Gashki CLI commands, validate responses, classify upstream errors
- internal/run: pass sequence and pass outcomes
- internal/store: atomic records, indexes, process ownership checks
- internal/batch: ordered queue and per-repository results
- internal/session: assigned Claude session IDs and saved-session opening
- prompts/, tests/stubs/, rr-run.sh (launcher only), README.md

Build an executable named rr-run. The old rr-run.sh becomes a short launcher for the installed executable (never compiles Go per run).
acceptance_criteria:
- The decision gate and all three phase epics are closed.
- Pass order 01, 02, 02.5, 03, 04, 05 is preserved; one Claude session serves all six passes of one run; pane placement and human handover are kept.
- Agent arguments use argument arrays and standard JSON encoding; paths with spaces and shell metacharacters work.
- Every completion wait starts from the returned turn cursor; lint failure is non-fatal and visible; each run saves a versioned checkpoint.
- Settings resolve flag > file > default; unknown keys, duplicate keys and invalid values are rejected with file, key and source line; no setting is read from environment variables; each run saves reusable rr-run and Gashki config records; the resolved Gashki state directory is queried, not computed.
- A batch runs repositories one at a time with an independent outcome per repository; repeated runs never replace earlier results; the original Claude session is saved and can be reopened without replaying review passes; batch recovery never silently repeats uncertain work.
- Read commands never launch agents or cause destructive effects.
- All behavior is verified with stub executables; no live agent run was needed.
- The Bash engine is gone (rr-run.sh is only a launcher). No yq or jq dependency remains in the Go runner. The Python output linter remains a dependency.

title: Settle open design decisions before implementation
description:
The rr-run Go conversion design contains choices that are recommendations, not approved decisions. Implementation tasks assume them. Building on an unapproved choice risks rework, so each choice needs an explicit accept or change before the baseline and module work starts. The written design has also had no independent review.

Already settled (not open): the default batch failure policy is continue-and-report for repository-specific failures (shared failures stop the batch); batch outputs stay directly in the repository's parent directory; agents in tests are stubs by default; any new live agent run and any release publication need explicit approval.
design:
Open choices and the draft recommendation for each:

- Use Go for rr-run, with github.com/pelletier/go-toml/v2 behind a small adapter. This replaces an earlier Bash plus yq plan and removes the yq dependency and the duplicate-key precheck.
- Write type-correct TOML records (context_1m = true; paths, models and durations as strings) instead of quoting every value. The earlier plan showed all values quoted yet declared context_1m boolean; reader and writer must agree.
- One sequential batch worker; no concurrent review runs.
- An explicit stop-on-failure mode in addition to the settled default.
- Phase-3 artifact filenames get a run-ID prefix (rr-<run-id>--) while staying directly in the repository's parent directory, so repeated runs do not replace earlier results.
- Assign a Claude session UUID before spawn instead of discovering it by guessing from the newest transcript.
- Open saved sessions through Gashki; send no review prompt on open.
- Keep completed panes open; automatic pane closure is outside this build.
- Batch restart continues queued repositories and does not automatically repeat an uncertain or interrupted pass.
- SEND_UNCERTAIN (a send whose delivery is unknown) defaults to handover, with no automatic resend.
- Two added rr-run settings: review_root and state_dir.
acceptance_criteria:
- Each choice above is recorded as accepted or changed, with the decision visible in a comment on this issue or its close reason.
- Every accepted change that differs from the draft is applied to the affected open issues (text updated) before this issue is closed.
- An independent review of the written design is done, or is explicitly waived in a recorded comment.
close_reason: All 11 choices accepted as drafted; independent design review waived by project owner. See comment. No other issue text needed changes.

title: Create Go module with command declarations and error registry
description: Parsing, help, introspection, documentation and error handling must all come from one declared command surface, one JSON envelope and one error/exit-code registry. If each is hand-written separately, they drift apart and callers cannot rely on them. Every later task builds on this one.
design:
Create the Go module under tools/rr-run/ (layout in the epic). Follow the make-cli CLI standard (revision 26f47a9a621862b63f3d7baccbb2ca7e441f5254; archetype: build/task orchestrator whose main task is a review run; important surfaces are a plan, per-run results, saved state, settings and recoverable errors). The rr-run rule that no setting comes from environment variables replaces make-cli's general env precedence. Profiles are outside this build. Any other departure from the standard must be recorded as a conflict and decided by the project owner before implementing.

Target command set (declare all; advertise only commands implemented so far in help, capabilities and docs):

- rr-run [settings flags] REPO (alias for run), rr-run run, rr-run plan REPO --json
- rr-run config show | get | validate | schema | set | patch | edit
- rr-run runs list | get
- rr-run batch run | plan | get | resume
- rr-run sessions list | get | open
- rr-run doctor, capabilities --json, schema NAME --json, robot-docs guide, feedback TEXT, --help, --version

Flag grammar: each flag declares arity and value type. Boolean setting flags take an explicit true or false so a flag can override a file's true value. Zero-argument selectors include --json, --toml, --help. Support --name=value and --name value. Reject duplicate flags. Honor -- as end of flags.

Output: JSON mode sends progress to stderr and exactly one final envelope to stdout, also on failure; the envelope has all seven make-cli keys and required metadata; rr-run contract version is 1; saved JSON records use a separate record_version = 1. No child process output may enter envelope stdout. Human mode shows pass progress, run ID, results and a session-open command; suppress colors and bells for non-terminal output, NO_COLOR and TERM=dumb.

Registry: declare verbs, flags, aliases, schemas, exit codes, error codes, setting sources and state transitions once; generate parsing and introspection from the same declarations where possible. Each error code declares its applicable verbs and a reproducible fixture. Follow make-cli's fixed diagnosis order (an unknown flag must not be hidden by a later missing repository) and pin ordering with compound-fault tests.

Exit codes: 0 success (including lint warnings or an empty read result); 1 invalid command input or setting value; 2 documented safety refusal; 3 missing dependency, unreadable input file or broken environment; 4 retry-safe read wait or lock attempt failed; 5 existing state or incompatible ownership conflicts; 6 rr-run internal defect; 7 review failed, uncertain or interrupted (handover required); 8 batch has at least one unsuccessful item. Never pass Gashki exit codes through to callers; Gashki's uncertain-send code must not be read as success.

Error codes: INVALID_INPUT, INVALID_CONFIG, UNKNOWN_FLAG, UNKNOWN_COMMAND, NOT_FOUND, CONFLICT, LOCKED, UPSTREAM_FAILURE, OUTPUT_MISSING, OUTPUT_CONFLICT, SEND_UNCERTAIN, RECOVERY_REQUIRED, SESSION_UNAVAILABLE, WAIT_TIMEOUT, CONFIG_UNWRITABLE, IDEMPOTENCY_CONFLICT, INTERNAL. Warnings: LINT_FAILED, ENV_SETTING_IGNORED, EVENT_LOG_UNAVAILABLE, SESSION_PERSISTENCE_UNAVAILABLE (where the operation can still succeed; for sessions open an unavailable session is an error).

Failure envelopes for a stopped run keep partial data: run ID, paths, upstream code, evidence and a safe next action. Malformed config errors name file, key if known, and source line. Flag errors name the flag, never an invented config line.

Run record schema (record_version 1) fields: record version, run ID, tool version, repository path, initial Git commit; artifact path, scratch path, review-root path, prompt hashes; lifecycle state, current pass, pass results, timestamps; Gashki selector, pane ID, opaque cursor, send key when known; resolved settings available so far with sources; last error, safe follow-up commands, process owner information; nullable agent_session (never a pane ID). Run states: prepared, spawning, running, waiting, approval, completed, failed, interrupted. Pass substates: prepared, sending, sent, checking, done.
acceptance_criteria:
- go build, go vet and go test pass for the new module.
- --help and --version work; help and capabilities list only implemented commands.
- Tests cover unknown flag, duplicate flag, -- handling, --name value versus --name=value, and explicit true/false booleans.
- JSON mode, including preflight errors, writes exactly one valid envelope to stdout and progress to stderr (case T116).
- A compound-fault test shows an unknown flag is reported before a missing repository.
- Every error code lists applicable verbs and has a reproducible fixture; exit-code mapping is tested; Gashki exit codes never reach callers.
- Record schema and state/substate enums exist in code with record_version 1.

title: Build Gashki client with response validation
description: rr-run controls agent panes only through the Gashki CLI. The Bash script trusted exit status and ad hoc parsing, so malformed output or a missing turn cursor could slip through. A zero exit does not excuse malformed JSON. Gashki's public CLI contract (contract 2, inspected at Gashki commit 8eaecc9) is the only boundary between the two programs.
design:
Put the client in internal/gashki. Do not import Gashki's internal packages and do not copy its private TOML parser.

- Run the executable with os/exec and argument slices; set cwd, stdin, stdout, stderr and env explicitly; never use sh -c with an assembled string. Keep the subprocess interface small so tests can inject stubs.
- Before any mutation, check Gashki's version and the required contract fields.
- For each command used (version, config get, config show --toml, spawn, send, wait including --since, observe, and others needed), validate JSON parse, the ok field, and the required data or error fields.
- Keep the Gashki error code and evidence in the rr-run error record; classify upstream errors into rr-run codes (UPSTREAM_FAILURE, SEND_UNCERTAIN, WAIT_TIMEOUT). Do not return Gashki exit codes to callers.
- Resolve the Gashki event-log path by running config get state_dir --json and reading data.value as an absolute path. Do not derive it from an env variable. (Phase 2 passes the selected Gashki config on that query.)
- Gashki's plain config show output is not TOML in the inspected implementation; config show --toml is the TOML form (used in phase 2).
- Temporary phase-1 compatibility: the GASHKI env variable still names the executable until phase 2 removes it.
acceptance_criteria:
- Malformed JSON, missing ok, or a missing cursor on send fails before any dependent action even when the process exit is zero (case T107).
- Stub tests record every call as a JSON argv array and verify exact arguments.
- Incompatible or missing contract fields refuse before mutation and name expected versus found.
- Gashki code and evidence appear in rr-run error records; Gashki exit codes are never passed through.
- A missing Gashki executable gives a missing-dependency error (exit 3).
close_reason: Moved to the rr-run project issue tracker (epic rr-run-7r7). No work was done here.

title: Build run state store with ownership locks
description: Batches, recovery and session reopening all depend on a durable per-run record written before any external action. The Bash script keeps no state. A crash between sending a prompt and recording it must be detectable so later code never replays a possibly delivered prompt.
design:
Put the store in internal/store.

- State root: $XDG_STATE_HOME/rr-run, else ~/.local/state/rr-run. An index points to run manifests. No credentials are stored.
- Before spawn, allocate a random run ID and create the run's checkpoint. Persist the record fields listed in the record schema (see the module/declarations task).
- Write checkpoints and the index atomically: same-directory temporary file, fsync, rename.
- Use an OS lock (flock) for the foreground owner. Another process cannot own the same run or the same repository at once. The OS releases the lock after a crash.
- A read can report lost ownership but must not silently rewrite the record.
- Enforce the run state transition table: prepared -> spawning|failed; spawning -> running|failed|interrupted; running -> waiting|completed|failed|interrupted; waiting -> running|approval|failed|interrupted; approval -> waiting|failed|interrupted; completed terminal; failed terminal for this batch attempt; interrupted needs human inspection. Save a pass substate (prepared, sending, sent, checking, done). Save intent before each external action and the result after. The table does not authorize replay of a sending pass after a crash.
- Inject storage faults and clocks through small interfaces. Compile fault seams only into test builds; production refuses test triggers.
acceptance_criteria:
- A checkpoint exists before spawn.
- A fault injected between temp write and rename leaves the previous record intact.
- A second worker for the same repository cannot spawn (case T115); a killed owner's lock is released by the OS.
- Invalid state transitions are rejected; the transition table is tested.
- Reading a lost-owner record reports lost ownership without rewriting it.
- go test -race passes for the ownership code.
- Records contain no credentials; agent_session is null in phase 1 and never holds a pane ID.

title: Handle pass outputs, lint results, and scratch cleanup
description: After each pass the agent writes Markdown review outputs. The Bash script found them with a one-second sleep and timestamps, could move tracked files, could overwrite existing results, and passed paths to the linter through shell word splitting. Wrong detection loses or clobbers review results, and an unchecked cleanup can delete files the run does not own.
design:
- Per pass, take a baseline of direct Markdown files in the repository and in the artifact directory. After the turn, compare size and content hash. Do not rely on a sleep or timestamp precision.
- Move a changed repository file into the artifact location only when Git confirms the file is untracked. Never move a tracked file.
- Never replace an existing artifact file. On a name conflict report OUTPUT_CONFLICT and keep both sources.
- Invoke the existing Python linter tools/lint_pass_outputs.py with one argument per output path (argument array). Save its exit code and diagnostics. Lint failure is a warning (LINT_FAILED); later passes still run. Failure to start the linter is an environment failure (exit 3), not a lint warning.
- No changed output is a run failure (OUTPUT_MISSING); keep the pane and scratch directory.
- Remove scratch only after all passes finish, only the directory this run created and recorded, after checking ownership and the resolved path. Refuse a symlink substitution. Never remove caller-owned files. In phase 1 the scratch directory is the same .rr-scratch location the Bash script used.
- In phase 1 outputs stay directly above the repository, as today.
acceptance_criteria:
- T108: no changed Markdown output -> run fails; pane and scratch remain.
- T109: a tracked Markdown file changed in the repo is never moved.
- T110: an untracked output whose destination exists is not overwritten; OUTPUT_CONFLICT reported and both files kept.
- T111: linter returns failure -> visible warning and later passes run.
- T112: linter cannot start -> environment failure.
- T114: scratch path replaced with a symlink -> cleanup refused.
- Existing Python linter fixture tests still pass.
close_reason: Moved to the rr-run project issue tracker (epic rr-run-7r7). No work was done here.

title: Build six-pass engine with send, wait, and approval handling
description: This is the core run loop: one Claude session works the six passes in order while rr-run sends each prompt, waits for the turn, and hands the human control on approval or failure. The Bash version had five defects in this loop (string-built JSON, word splitting, sed path corruption, env-derived event path, unchecked approval-change wait). The Go version must keep the behavior and fix them.
design:
Put the loop in internal/run.

- Passes in order: 01, 02, 02.5, 03, 04, 05. One pane and one Claude session for all six. Keep the current pane placement (agent pane beside the current pane; a tmux pane is required), human handover, model default (sonnet), permission mode (bypassPermissions), 1M-context override, added directories, and folder-trust response behavior unchanged.
- Render prompt placeholders by literal string replacement (no sed, no regex substitution of paths). Build the whole agent argument array with encoding/json. Set Claude's cwd to the repository.
- Check Gashki's version and contract before mutation. Use selector rr-<repo-basename>/analyst and reject an existing pane.
- Per pass: persist the rendered prompt and its hash before send. Use stable key rr:<run-id>:<pass>. Reuse a key only with exactly the same pane, session and prompt bytes. After a confirmed send persist the opaque turn cursor and key, then wait with --since <cursor>. Never replace that with an unqualified idle wait.
- On approval: record the evidence cursor, notify the human to answer in the agent pane, check the result of the change wait, then return to the idle wait. rr-run never approves for the human.
- Uncertain send: keep the send key and any barrier cursor, do not resend, hand over with SEND_UNCERTAIN.
- Wait timeout, approval failure, dead pane or turn failure: preserve the pane, checkpoint, logs and scratch directory and hand over with the matching code.
- Keep rr-run.log entries for lint results, approvals and compactions. Leave the agent pane open after success or failure.
- Temporary phase-1 settings compatibility: keep reading RR_MODEL, RR_WAIT, RR_PROMPTS and GASHKI, marked temporary in the test fixture. Phase 2 removes them.
acceptance_criteria:
- T101: normal six-pass run -> pass order and prompt bytes match the baseline fixtures.
- T102: paths with space, quote, ampersand, dollar and backslash -> exact argv and literal prompt paths.
- T103: every completion wait uses the cursor returned by the matching send.
- T104: approval then change -> checked change result, then the wait continues.
- T105: failed change wait -> handover; the next prompt is not sent.
- T106: uncertain send -> no automatic resend; evidence recorded.
- The Go and old runners produce equivalent prompts and relevant spawn/send/wait arguments on normal fixtures.
close_reason: Moved to the rr-run project issue tracker (epic rr-run-7r7). No work was done here.

title: Handle interrupts and lost owners
description: If rr-run is stopped or killed after it decided to send a prompt, the prompt may or may not have reached the agent. Treating that pass as unstarted would duplicate a review prompt in a live session. The record must preserve the uncertainty.
design:
- On SIGINT or SIGTERM: stop new sends, save interruption state when possible, leave agent panes intact. Stopping a Gashki wait does not stop the agent.
- On uncatchable termination, the next owner treats a lost-owner record in an active state as interrupted and does not assume the pass never ran.
- Interrupted outcome exits with code 7 and retains partial data and safe follow-up commands in the failure envelope.
- Provide signal injection points only in test builds.
acceptance_criteria:
- T113: interrupt after send intent -> saved uncertainty; no automatic replay.
- SIGINT and SIGTERM leave the agent pane running and the checkpoint readable.
- A record left active by a killed owner is reported as interrupted by the next reader or owner, without replaying any pass.
close_reason: Moved to the rr-run project issue tracker (epic rr-run-7r7). No work was done here.

title: Add plan, runs, doctor, and introspection commands
description: Humans and calling scripts need to see what a run would do, find earlier runs, and check dependencies without starting any agent. These commands are read-only; any read that launched an agent or mutated state would break the rule that reads are safe.
design:
- plan [settings flags] REPO --json: read-only. Return resolved settings, pass order, output paths, required dependencies and proposed agent arguments. Launch no agent. For a new run show a run-ID placeholder; allocate no state.
- runs list [--limit=N] [--cursor=CURSOR] [--json]: default 25 entries, at most 100 per call, sorted by saved creation time descending then ID ascending. Use opaque pagination cursors with a frozen upper bound. Reject a cursor used against another list or filter.
- runs get RUN_ID [--wait] [--wait-timeout=DURATION] [--json]: --wait observes an existing run and never creates a worker. A failed retry-safe wait gives exit 4.
- doctor [--json]: dependency checks (Gashki executable and contract, Python linter, tmux, writable state root). Never start an agent to check help or version.
- capabilities --json, schema NAME --json, robot-docs guide: generated from the declarations registry.
- feedback TEXT: writes locally under the rr-run state root; sends no message and makes no network request; never copies prompts or credentials into the file.
- Reads never rewrite records and never have destructive effects.
acceptance_criteria:
- plan, runs list/get, doctor, capabilities, schema and robot-docs launch no agent and change no run record.
- Pagination: default 25, maximum 100, stable order, cursor frozen, cursor reuse against another list rejected.
- runs get --wait attaches to an existing run and never spawns a worker.
- feedback writes only a local file and makes no network call.
- Plan output contains no allocated run ID.
close_reason: Moved to the rr-run project issue tracker (epic rr-run-7r7). No work was done here.

title: Replace launcher, write guide, and verify phase 1 with stubs
description: Callers still invoke tools/rr-run/rr-run.sh. After conversion that file must become a thin launcher so there is one implementation of each pass and run transition, not a second Bash engine. This task also runs the phase-1 completion checks.
design:
- rr-run.sh becomes a short launcher for the installed rr-run executable. It resolves its own real path to find the repo-review root, accepts an explicit --review-root=PATH override, never compiles Go on each run, and when the executable is missing prints a precise installation command.
- Document the build and install command, the guide (robot-docs guide) and the README. Keep the old script only until equivalence is proven against the baseline fixtures, then remove the Bash engine.
- Run: Go tests, go vet, ShellCheck and shell syntax check of the launcher, the existing Python output-linter and template-linter fixture tests, and the equivalence comparison against baseline fixtures.
- Archive baseline observations; delete unused temporary programs and databases.

- The launcher works from a symlinked path, honors --review-root, and prints a precise install command when the executable is missing; ShellCheck is clean.
- No Bash engine remains; one implementation exists of each pass and run transition.
- All phase-1 acceptance criteria hold: equivalent prompts and relevant spawn/send/wait arguments, defect regressions pass, help/envelopes/records/error registry tests pass, existing linter fixture tests pass.
- Cases T101 to T116 pass.

title: Phase 2 - Reform rr-run configuration
description: rr-run settings come only from four environment variables. The layered design needs: L1 (rr-run) owns job and agent choices; L2 (Gashki) owns pane control, hooks, state paths and other mechanism settings; L0 owns identity, authentication and vendor config roots. Each layer has its own TOML file, setting order is flag > file > default, and each run saves its resolved settings so the run can be repeated. This phase builds the rr-run side of that design.
design: Child tasks: prove the TOML adapter first, then typed settings resolution with read-only config verbs, then write verbs (set/patch/edit) and Gashki snapshots in parallel, then round trips, contract and guide. Do not change Gashki's own config specification or source in this phase; Gashki's parser swap is separate work and rr-run does not depend on it.

- All phase-2 test cases T201 to T222 (listed in the child tasks) pass.
- A saved config record round-trips: resolved values, types and relevant agent arguments are preserved, and sources become file.
- Changing the original config after a run starts does not change that run.
- Retired setting variables cannot change any run setting.
- No yq or jq dependency remains in the Go runner. The Python output linter remains a dependency.

title: Prove the TOML adapter
description: Config commands must report errors by file, key and source line, reject duplicate and unknown keys, and edit values without disturbing comments. The chosen library, github.com/pelletier/go-toml/v2, exposes source positions in its stable decoder errors, but its source-node API lives in an unstable package without compatibility guarantees. Feasibility must be proven before config commands depend on it.
design:
Build a small adapter in internal/config. Use the library decoder for TOML grammar, duplicate detection and types. Keep original bytes and library-derived source ranges for provenance and comment-preserving edits. Confine the unstable API to the adapter, pin the module version, and test source ranges. Do not assume ordinary decode-and-encode preserves comments. The documentation was inspected at v2.4.3; select and pin a verified version at implementation and do not claim it is the latest.

Prove the adapter can: (1) reject duplicate keys and unknown keys; (2) identify the line of a well-formed but semantically invalid value; (3) identify the source range of a multiline string; (4) replace a scalar value without changing unrelated bytes; (5) reject unsupported syntax before it can affect source mapping.

If the proof fails, record the failure and revise the library choice with the project owner. Do not replace the library with a custom TOML parser and do not drop line diagnostics.
acceptance_criteria:
- A passing test exists for each of the five proofs.
- The pinned go-toml version is recorded in go.mod; only the adapter imports the unstable package.
- If any proof fails, the issue is not closed and the failure is reported with the evidence.
close_reason: Moved to the rr-run project issue tracker (epic rr-run-7r7). No work was done here.

title: Resolve typed settings with provenance and read-only config verbs
description: Environment variables are not a systematic or inspectable configuration surface. Users need a TOML file per layer, flag > file > default resolution, clear errors with line numbers, and a way to see where each value came from.
design:
Settings (key, TOML type, default, flag):

- model: string, sonnet, --model
- wait_timeout: duration string, 2h, --wait-timeout
- prompts: path string, <review-root>/tools/rr-run/prompts, --prompts
- gashki_bin: executable string, gashki, --gashki-bin
- gashki_config: path string, empty (use Gashki's default), --gashki-config
- permission_mode: string, bypassPermissions, --permission-mode
- context_1m: boolean, true, --context-1m
- review_root: path string, discovered installation root, --review-root
- state_dir: path string, rr-run XDG state root, --state-dir

review_root and state_dir belong to rr-run and do not override Gashki's state dir. The pass list, agent type, placement, trust response and added-directory rules stay in code; add no arbitrary agent-argument escape hatch.

Resolution and files:
- --config=PATH selects the rr-run file; else $XDG_CONFIG_HOME/rr-run/config.toml, else ~/.config/rr-run/config.toml. A missing default file means defaults. A missing explicit file is INVALID_CONFIG. An empty explicit file is valid. config validate PATH fails when PATH is absent. set, patch and edit (separate task) may create the selected file.
- Validate the whole file before applying flags; a flag cannot hide an invalid file value. Track source (flag, file or default) for every setting; file sources carry the absolute path and 1-based line.
- Reject unknown keys and tables (profiles are reserved, not accepted). Keys are snake_case, one direct key per setting; reject dotted keys and quoted key spellings. Valid TOML string forms are fine; never parse values with regexes. File limit 1 MiB; reject invalid UTF-8 and non-regular inputs.
- wait_timeout: Go duration, 1s through 24h (Gashki's single-wait limit). permission_mode: default, acceptEdits, plan, auto, dontAsk, bypassPermissions. Pass the 1M setting to the agent explicitly as 0 for true and 1 for false.
- Executable value without a path separator is a PATH lookup name; with a separator it is a path. File-sourced relative paths resolve against the config file's directory; flag-sourced relative paths against the invocation cwd; computed defaults from the installation and XDG roots. No shell-variable or ~ expansion inside TOML strings.
- Remove the temporary env inputs RR_MODEL, RR_WAIT, RR_PROMPTS and GASHKI as settings. Keep OS conventions and vendor identity roots; keep Gashki's internal spawn-to-hook values; never strip vendor identity from the child environment.

Verbs:
- config show: plain output is valid TOML with a header and source comments; --toml is the same; --toml --json is INVALID_INPUT; --json returns typed config plus _provenance in the standard envelope. Fixed key order; strings encoded by the TOML library.
- config get KEY [--json]; config validate [PATH] [--json] (never launches Gashki or an agent); config schema --json (types, bounds, defaults, path rules, additionalProperties false). Suggest a near-match for an unknown key only when one is justified.
acceptance_criteria:
- T201: no default file -> defaults and default sources.
- T202: missing explicit file -> INVALID_CONFIG before spawn.
- T203: empty named file -> defaults, valid file.
- T204: file model plus --model -> flag wins; exact source recorded.
- T205: unknown, duplicate or table key -> rejected with location.
- T206: wrong type or invalid duration -> file, key, line and accepted domain reported.
- T207: relative path in a config file -> resolved from the config directory.
- T208: relative path from a flag -> resolved from the invocation cwd.
- T209: TOML escapes, Unicode and multiline strings -> correct value and source range.
- The Go runner reads no setting from RR_MODEL, RR_WAIT, RR_PROMPTS or GASHKI.
close_reason: Moved to the rr-run project issue tracker (epic rr-run-7r7). No work was done here.

title: Add config set, patch, and edit
description: Users need to change settings without hand-editing in ways that destroy comments or lose concurrent edits. Scripts need an atomic, validated JSON patch path.
design:
- set KEY VALUE [--json]: parse VALUE by KEY's declared type.
- patch --from-stdin [--json]: read a JSON object from stdin (limit 1 MiB). Reject unknown keys, wrong types, null, duplicate JSON keys and trailing JSON. An empty patch creates an empty target if it is absent.
- Apply all changes atomically after validation. Preserve unrelated comments, whitespace and key order (use the adapter's source ranges). Use a cooperative file lock and compare original bytes before rename; refuse an observed concurrent change (CONFLICT/LOCKED). Unwritable target: CONFIG_UNWRITABLE.
- edit: requires terminal input. Invoke EDITOR by argument vector (never through a shell) using a documented editor-argument parser, with vi as fallback. Open a temporary working copy and validate it before replacing the target. On validation failure keep the working copy and report its path. Refuse a target that changed while the editor was open.
- set, patch and edit may create the selected file even when it is missing (exception to the missing-explicit-file error). Output reports whether the file was created.
acceptance_criteria:
- T217: set/patch creation and empty patch -> correct created flag and target bytes.
- T218: set/patch on a commented file -> unrelated bytes unchanged.
- T219: invalid JSON patch or duplicate-key JSON patch -> target unchanged.
- T220: concurrent config edit -> conflict reported; no lost update.
- T221: edit without a terminal, and --toml with --json -> clear INVALID_INPUT.
close_reason: Moved to the rr-run project issue tracker (epic rr-run-7r7). No work was done here.

title: Snapshot configs into runs and query the Gashki state directory
description: A run that cannot be repeated or audited is hard to trust. Each run must save the rr-run settings and the Gashki config it actually used, and rr-run must read Gashki's event log from the state directory Gashki really uses.
design:
- Resolve gashki_config once. Pass it on every Gashki call when supplied.
- Query config get state_dir --json; read data.value as an absolute path; use it for events.jsonl. Never compute it from GASHKI_STATE_DIR.
- Before spawn, save rr-run.config.toml and gashki.config.toml beside rr-run.log. Obtain the Gashki record with config show --toml (plain config show is not TOML in the inspected implementation). Check both output and exit status. Fail before spawn if either record fails.
- Set the rr-run record's gashki_config to the recorded Gashki file's absolute path, and use that recorded file for all mutating Gashki calls in the run. Both records must exist and be readable before any agent starts. Use typed values and absolute resolved paths. Exclude run IDs, session IDs, timestamps and secrets from setting keys.
- A record pins tool-controlled settings, not repository contents or vendor identity. A rerun gets a new run ID and a new session. It does not reproduce later changes to agent binaries, auth, MCP settings, prompt files or source code; record versions and prompt hashes separately.
- Gashki omits an unset tmux socket from its TOML; preserve that omission. It means the current TMUX/default server is used, not a pinned server. Record the observed pane target separately and invent no socket setting.
- doctor warns (ENV_SETTING_IGNORED) when RR_MODEL, RR_WAIT, RR_PROMPTS or GASHKI is set, naming the replacement flag. Missing or unreadable event log gives the EVENT_LOG_UNAVAILABLE warning.
acceptance_criteria:
- T211: retired env names set -> no setting effect; doctor warns with replacement flags.
- T212: Gashki file names a custom state dir -> the correct event log is read.
- T213: all Gashki operations use the saved Gashki config.
- T214: a config record cannot be written -> no agent spawn.
- T215: source config file changes after the run starts -> the frozen run settings stay in use.
- T222: unset Gashki socket -> setting omitted; the ambient-server limit is documented.

title: Finish config round trips and contract and guide

title: Phase 3 - Add batches and saved sessions
description: A run handles one repository and leaves no way back into the review conversation. Users need to review a series of repositories in one batch, keep every run's results separate, and open the original Claude review session later to discuss the results with the agent, without re-running passes or starting a blank session.
design: Child tasks: unique prefixed artifacts and index; session UUID assignment and pane ownership; idempotency keys; batch input parsing and preflight; batch queue with failure policy; batch resume; saved session inspection; discussion-pane open; fault tests/contracts/guide; complete-build checks.

- All phase-3 test cases T301 to T325 (listed in the child tasks) pass with stubs.
- Batch inputs, isolated artifacts, saved results, partial failures, restart and session opening pass the stub tests.
- Session open uses the original UUID and identity root, including after the original pane is removed in the fixture.
- No automatic recovery path duplicates a possibly delivered review prompt.

title: Give each run unique prefixed artifacts and index discovery
description: Two runs against the same repository currently write the same output names in the same place, so a later run replaces an earlier review. Batches make that worse. Results must be kept side by side in the repository's parent directory (the chosen location), and every run must be discoverable later even if the index is stale.
design:
Use the repository's parent directory as the artifact root for single runs and batch items. Create no output subdirectory. Do not use the repository basename alone as run identity.

In phase 3 prefix each run file with rr-<run-id>-- directly in the parent directory:

- rr-<run-id>--run.json, rr-<run-id>--rr-run.config.toml, rr-<run-id>--gashki.config.toml, rr-<run-id>--rr-run.log
- rr-<run-id>--01-first-read.md, --02-discounted-artifact.md, --02.5-synthesis.md, --03-trace.md, --04-twin.md, --05-lift.md
- rr-<run-id>--pass-01.prompt.txt, rr-<run-id>--pass-01.lint.log, and the same prompt and lint files for every pass

Record complete output paths and hashes in the run manifest and the complete prefixed Gashki config path in the rr-run config record. Emit no unprefixed compatibility copies (they would be ambiguous after another run). Leave existing phase-1/2 outputs untouched. Explain the filename change in the guide and migration notes.

Before each pass, give the agent the exact output path for that pass and the paths of prior outputs from the same run, by updating the template output placeholder. A pass must not read another run's similarly named result by guessing a basename. Update the prompts that name outputs or tell the agent to write above the repository consistently; keep review content and pass labels unchanged.

Scratch directory: <repo-parent>/.rr-scratch-<run-id>/ holding temporary comparison clones, not review outputs. Keep it on handover; remove it only after complete success.

Overwrite rules: refuse a pre-existing target at run creation. Once a pass is recorded complete, never overwrite its result. If a user edits or removes a file, report a hash mismatch or missing file rather than reconstructing it silently.

Index: keep an atomic index of run ID to manifest path under the rr-run state root, plus batch manifests. The run manifest is authoritative; the index is a discovery aid. A stale or missing artifact target produces a precise error and is never silently omitted from runs get or sessions get.

Migration: move older checkpoint locations into the index with an atomic index update. Preserve their original artifact paths and nullable session field. Never invent a session UUID for a phase-1/2 run that recorded none.

title: Assign session UUID and enforce pane ownership
description: Gashki identifies a pane, not a Claude session, and discards the vendor session_id from hooks. To let a human reopen a review later, rr-run must choose the Claude session ID itself before the agent starts and save it. Guessing the session from the newest transcript would be unreliable. New runs also need pane identities that cannot collide with a pane from an earlier run on the same repository.
design:
Session assignment:
- Generate a valid random UUID before the first spawn of each phase-3 run. Persist it before any mutation. Pass it through Gashki agent arguments as --session-id=<uuid>. Keep all six passes in that session.
- Claude documents --session-id (supply a UUID) and --resume (resume a specific session). These are separate from Gashki pane identifiers. Confirm the supported flags during dependency checks without starting an agent.
- Save: agent claude and the requested UUID; state requested, started or unavailable; repository cwd and the resolved CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR (including its default path); initial model, permission mode, 1M setting and required added directories; Gashki pane ID, selector and target when known; agent version when available without a live call; last observed live state and observation time.
- A successful spawn readiness proves the launch completed, not that a future transcript will remain available. Do not label an assigned UUID as a proven permanent session.
- Do not copy auth files, vendor settings or transcripts into run artifacts. The L0 config root is recorded as identity context, not as an rr-run setting.
- If session persistence is disabled in the caller environment, report SESSION_PERSISTENCE_UNAVAILABLE before spawn and refuse the run. Treat it as a dependency check; never change the user's identity or vendor settings automatically. An explicit disabled-persistence setting is a preflight error. A transcript removed after a completed run is a later availability error (for sessions open).

Pane ownership:
- New runs use selector rr-<run-id>/analyst (phase 1 used rr-<repo-basename>/analyst). An existing phase-3 selector is reusable only when the saved run proves it owns that exact pane; Gashki's existing result alone does not prove ownership.
- Before a new automated run, under the repository lock, inspect known rr-run pane references for that repository. A prior working, compacting or approval pane blocks the new run even if its foreground owner has exited. Report its saved run ID and target. Do not kill it, and do not assume it is idle because its manifest says failed. An unrelated completed idle pane does not block a run with a distinct phase-3 selector.

- T308: new run spawn -> UUID saved first, then passed as --session-id.
- T319: session persistence disabled -> preflight refuses before spawn.
- T325: an earlier live pane still working in the same repository -> new automated run refused with the earlier run ID and target.
- A pane found by an existing selector without a saved ownership proof is not reused.

title: Add idempotency keys for run creation
description: A caller that times out cannot tell whether a run was created. Without an idempotency key, retrying creates a second review and possibly a duplicate agent session. A key plus a hash of the resolved request lets a retry return the existing run safely.
design: Run and batch creation accept --idempotency-key=KEY. Under the creation lock, save the key and a hash of the resolved request before starting work. Repeating the same key and request returns the existing ID and state. A changed request with that key is IDEMPOTENCY_CONFLICT (exit 5). Without a key, an explicit run command creates a new run; the result reports the key and ID a caller can use for later checks. Never infer retry identity from a repository path alone. Never describe a new run invocation as a safe retry of an existing run. (Batch creation uses the same mechanism and is wired in the batch queue task.)

- T323 (run part): same key and changed request -> IDEMPOTENCY_CONFLICT, exit 5.

title: Parse and preflight batch input
description: A batch should fail early on bad input and never start a partial series of agents because of an input mistake found halfway through. Everything checkable before the first spawn must be checked before the first spawn.
design:
--repos-file names a UTF-8 file with one repository path per line. Ignore blank lines and lines whose first character is #. Remove a trailing CR from CRLF input. Preserve other path characters. Do not interpret quotes, escapes, globs, variables or shell commands. Resolve relative paths against the list file's directory. Reject newline characters in a repository path. List limit 1 MiB.

Reject an empty list and duplicate repositories after canonicalization. Require a readable Git repository for each item and keep the existing parent-directory-name rule. Never create, clone, move or repair repositories. Freeze the resolved queue before the batch starts.

Preflight every item, prompt, dependency, config and output destination before the first spawn. Initial input errors start no agents. A repository that becomes unavailable after preflight gets its own failure later. All items use one resolved setting set; per-repository overrides and multiple agent types are outside this build.

batch plan --repos-file=PATH [settings flags] --json is read-only: it shows the frozen queue, resolved settings and per-item destinations and launches no agent.
acceptance_criteria:
- T302: an invalid later input or a duplicate canonical repository -> no first spawn.
- Comments, blank lines, CRLF and relative paths parse as described; quotes and globs stay literal.
- Empty list and an over-1-MiB list are rejected.
- batch plan launches no agent and allocates no state.

title: Run the batch queue with failure policy
description: A user wants to review a series of repositories without babysitting each one. One bad repository must not hide the results of the others, and shared failures must not look like many repository failures.
design:
Commands: batch run --repos-file=PATH [--failure-policy=continue|stop] [settings flags], batch get BATCH_ID [--json]; batch creation accepts --idempotency-key as described in the run idempotency task.

- Create the batch ID and all run IDs before starting the first item. Save the queue, the list-file hash, the failure policy, the settings and per-item state in a batch manifest under the state root.
- Run one item at a time. Start the next item only after success or handover.
- Default policy continue: move to the next item after a repository-specific failure. Policy stop: leave later items queued. Shared failures always stop the batch once, with the shared cause: unwritable state, unavailable Gashki or tmux, invalid contract, corrupt state.
- An approval pauses the current item (run state approval) and rr-run never approves automatically; single-run approval behavior applies unchanged. A wait timeout hands that item to the human and may allow the next item in continue mode. Its agent may still be working; mark that in the batch result. Do not describe continue mode as limiting all live agents to one.
- A completed batch with any failed or interrupted item exits 8. Lint warnings alone do not fail a batch.
- The final report lists run ID, repository, outcome, artifact path and session status for every item, including queued items left after an early stop. For a partial failure the envelope includes all item results.
- Batch states: prepared, running, stopped, completed, interrupted. Item states: the run states plus queued and skipped. Record a reason for every stopped, failed, interrupted or skipped state.
- Same repository in separate batches gets distinct run IDs and artifacts.
acceptance_criteria:
- T301: three valid repositories -> frozen input order; one scheduled item at a time.
- T303: repository-specific failure, continue -> later items run; batch exits nonzero (8).
- T304: same failure, stop -> later items remain queued.
- T305: shared failure -> the batch stops once with the shared cause.
- T306: same repository in separate batches -> distinct IDs and independent artifacts.
- The final report lists every item, including queued ones, with run ID, repo, outcome, artifact path and session status.
